claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa material is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
Mo will be added to TiVNbTa as the intervention.
Adding Mo to TiVNbTa will form a stable solid solution.
The Mo-containing solid solution will produce solid-solution strengthening.
Solid-solution strengthening will enhance elevated-temperature strength retention.
Mo alloying will improve the high-temperature mechanical stability of TiVNbTa.
Mo-alloyed TiVNbTa will have a yield strength exceeding 400 MPa at 1273 K.
Mo-alloyed TiVNbTa will have a compressive strength exceeding 400 MPa at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a yield strength of 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K.
The proposed performance boundary extends to 1273 K and 30% strain.
Mo alloying may alter phase constitution or cause a ductility tradeoff.
The hypothesis will be tested by preparing Mo-alloyed TiVNbTa and measuring its high-temperature yield strength, compressive strength, and microstructure.
A yield strength or compressive strength below 400 MPa at 1273 K will falsify the hypothesis.
Significant degradation of ductility will falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The compressive-strength prediction is described as an improvement while requiring only a value above 400 MPa, but the stated baseline is already 423 MPa. A result between 400 and 423 MPa would satisfy the numerical prediction while representing deterioration.

The falsification threshold does not consistently test improvement relative to baseline: compressive strengths from 400 to 423 MPa would neither trigger falsification nor improve upon the stated 423 MPa baseline.
